description.value: The study investigated self-reference effects on source memory in Alzheimer's disease, behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia and healthy controls, and examined voxel-based morphometry correlates in cortical midline structures.

value: We hypothesised that the SRE for source memory would be comparably attenuated in bvFTD and AD, but that these deficits would be associated with an anterior-posterior dissociation of CMS atrophy.
Specifically, we proposed that atrophy of anterior-ventral CMS subregions would relate to the limited benefit of self-referential encoding on source memory retrieval in bvFTD.
On the other hand, we predicted that the reduced SRE in AD would be associated with atrophy in the posterior CMS subregions.

spans.text: The current version assessed source memory recognition following self-reference and other-reference encoding conditions. A perceptual condition was included as a control condition.
Self-reference condition
During the training and experimental encoding phases of the study, participants performed encoding tasks under three conditions (self-reference, other-reference and perceptual).

Other-reference condition

description.value: Participants judged whether Queen Elizabeth II would like the object-background pairing.

Perceptual condition

description.value: Participants judged whether the object and background contained similar colours.

spans.text: Participants judged whether the object and background contained similar colours (yes/no).
To minimize task-switching costs, trials were presented in blocks of 10 trials per encoding condition.
The self-reference source memory task was programmed using E-Prime 2.0 software (Psychology Software Tools, Pittsburgh, PA), and testing was conducted on a laptop with a 14-inch LED-backlit display.
During testing, participants provided verbal responses, which were recorded by the experimenter using the programmed response keys.

instructions.value: Participants judged whether they liked each object-background pairing under self-reference; whether Queen Elizabeth II would like it under other-reference; or whether the object and background contained similar colours under the perceptual condition. At test, they judged each object old, new, or don't know, followed by the background source as mountain, beach, or don't know for objects judged old.

stimuli.value: Colour images of 30 common objects superimposed on one of two colour landscape background scenes (mountain or beach), plus 10 novel objects; Queen Elizabeth II's photograph was shown for the other-reference instructions.
